# adds_acl (Resource)

Manages the **complete** discretionary ACL (DACL) of an Active Directory object.

This resource is **authoritative**: every explicit, non-inherited ACE on `target` that is not declared here is removed on apply. ACEs are matched by identity rather than position, so Active Directory's own ACE ordering never produces a permanent diff. The **Protect object from accidental deletion** ACE (a `Deny` for `Everyone` on `Delete`/`DeleteTree`) and inherited ACEs are always preserved and never reported as drift.

Because it owns the whole DACL, do not point an `adds_ace` at the same `target`: the next apply of this resource would prune it. The recommended way to onboard an existing object is to `terraform import` it first, so every current ACE is captured before you edit.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "adds_organizational_unit" "servers" {
  path = "Contoso/Servers"
}

resource "adds_group" "server_admins" {
  name  = "Server Admins"
  path  = "Contoso/Groups"
  scope = "DomainLocal"
}

# Authoritative DACL for the OU. This resource owns every explicit ACE on the OU - any
# explicit ACE not declared below is removed on apply - while inherited ACEs and the
# always-preserved "Protect from accidental deletion" ACE are left in place. Set
# inheritance_blocked = true to additionally break inheritance.
resource "adds_acl" "servers" {
  target = adds_organizational_unit.servers.distinguished_name

  # Server admins can create and delete computer objects in the OU.
  ace {
    trustee               = adds_group.server_admins.sid
    rights                = ["CreateChild", "DeleteChild"]
    object_type           = "computer"
    inherited_object_type = "organizationalUnit"
    inheritance           = "Descendents"
  }

  # ... and write any property on those computer objects.
  ace {
    trustee               = adds_group.server_admins.sid
    rights                = ["WriteProperty"]
    object_type           = "All"
    inherited_object_type = "computer"
    inheritance           = "Descendents"
  }

  # Authenticated users may read the subtree.
  ace {
    trustee     = "Authenticated Users"
    rights      = ["GenericRead"]
    inheritance = "All"
  }

  # Deny resetting user passwords in the subtree.
  ace {
    trustee               = "Authenticated Users"
    access                = "Deny"
    rights                = ["ExtendedRight"]
    object_type           = "Reset Password"
    inherited_object_type = "user"
    inheritance           = "Descendents"
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `target` (String) Object whose DACL is managed. Accepts a slash-delimited path relative to the domain root (for example `Servers` or `Contoso/Servers`), a relative distinguished name such as `CN=Computers`, or a full distinguished name. Slash segments are always OU names. The object does not need to be managed by Terraform.

### Optional

- `ace` (Attributes List) The complete set of explicit ACEs for `target`. Omit, or set to an empty list, to declare that the object has no explicit ACEs (beyond the always-preserved accidental-deletion ACE). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--ace))
- `ignore_admin_count_1` (Boolean) Allow managing the DACL even when `target` has `adminCount = 1` (protected by AdminSDHolder). By default this is an error, because SDProp periodically resets the ACL of any adminCount=1 object to match AdminSDHolder, silently discarding the ACEs this resource wrote.
- `inheritance_blocked` (Boolean) Break inheritance on `target` so only the declared ACEs (and the accidental-deletion ACE) apply. Defaults to `false`, which keeps inheritance enabled: this resource still owns the explicit ACEs but leaves inherited ones in place. Set to `true` to break inheritance, in which case inherited ACEs are dropped rather than copied down as explicit ACEs. On destroy, inheritance is re-enabled only if this resource broke it.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Terraform resource identifier, equal to the resolved distinguished name of `target`.
- `target_dn` (String) Resolved distinguished name of `target`.

<a id="nestedatt--ace"></a>
### Nested Schema for `ace`

Required:

- `rights` (Set of String) `ActiveDirectoryRights` values combined into a single ACE, for example `["CreateChild", "DeleteChild"]`.
- `trustee` (String) Principal the ACE grants or denies rights to. Accepts a SID, a distinguished name, `DOMAIN\name`, a `sAMAccountName`, or a well-known name such as `Authenticated Users`.

Optional:

- `access` (String) `Allow` or `Deny`. Defaults to `Allow`.
- `inheritance` (String) `ActiveDirectorySecurityInheritance`: `None`, `All`, `Descendents`, `SelfAndChildren` or `Children`. Omitting it applies the ACE to the target object only.
- `inherited_object_type` (String) Schema class of the child objects that inherit this ACE, for example `organizationalUnit`. Requires `inheritance`.
- `object_type` (String) Object the rights apply to: a schema class (`computer`), an attribute or property set, an extended right, a GUID, or `All`. Omit for rights that are not object-specific.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# An authoritative ACL is imported by the target's distinguished name. Importing first
# captures every current explicit ACE, so you can review them before editing - this resource
# prunes any explicit ACE you do not keep in the configuration.
terraform import adds_acl.servers "OU=Servers,OU=Contoso,DC=contoso,DC=local"
```
